data.body:
BLOCKED — `terraform apply` cannot run. STOPPED before applying. The blocker is a PRE-EXISTING
defect on `main`, unrelated to this change, that makes the whole `infra/terraform` root module
un-plannable for everyone.

## What happens

    cd infra/terraform && terraform init   # OK, S3 backend configured
    terraform plan -out=...

    Error: Error in function call
      on main.tf line 63, in resource "aws_instance" "gerrit":
      63:   user_data = templatefile("${path.module}/user_data.sh", { ... })
    Call to function "templatefile" failed: ./user_data.sh:92,24-25: Invalid
    character; This character is not used within the language., and 3 other diagnostic(s).

A `-target`ed plan restricted to the four SSM parameters fails identically — terraform evaluates
the whole configuration before it applies `-target`, so there is no narrow path through it.

## Root cause

Commit `ef1a7e66a65d` ("Gate standalone shell scripts with ShellCheck", already merged to main)
added explanatory comments to `infra/terraform/user_data.sh`. Each comment escapes its FIRST
mention of a bash brace expansion as `$${...}` but leaves the "reduces to" / "becomes" half
UNESCAPED, so `templatefile()` tries to parse it as HCL and `!` / `[$name]` are invalid there.

Three sites, all inside `#` comments (harmless to bash, fatal to templatefile):

    line  92: # reduces to ${!PARAMS[@]} / ${PARAMS[$name]}. ShellCheck reads the escaped pre-render
                            ^^^^^^^^^^^^^   ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
    line 111: # After rendering, "$${!PARAMS[@]}" becomes "${!PARAMS[@]}" — one word per key.
                                                           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^

Fix is to write them `$${!PARAMS[@]}` / `$${PARAMS[$name]}` like the lines above them do.
`infra/terraform/user_data.sh` is byte-identical between this branch and `origin/main`, and
`0f1d0cfc7792` does not touch it — confirmed by `diff` against `git show origin/main:...`.

Not fixed here: it is an unrelated file, it belongs in its own reviewed change, and editing a
production `user_data` input as a drive-by during a credentials apply is not a call to make
unilaterally. Filing it as a separate bug is the right move — it currently blocks ALL terraform
work on this box, not just this ticket.

Blast radius when it IS fixed (checked so the fixer is not surprised): `aws_instance.gerrit` has
`lifecycle { ignore_changes = [ami] }` and does NOT set `user_data_replace_on_change`, which
defaults to `false` in AWS provider v5. So the corrected `user_data` shows as an in-place attribute
update, not a destroy/recreate of the production Gerrit instance. Worth re-reading in the real plan
rather than trusting this note.

## State and preconditions, established before stopping

- State is REMOTE: S3 `rebar-tfstate-896586841071`, key `rebar/prod/terraform.tfstate`,
  region `us-east-1`, `encrypt = true`, `use_lockfile = true` (S3-native locking, no DynamoDB).
  `terraform init` succeeded and the backend is reachable; providers resolved
  (aws 5.100.0, random 3.9.0, archive 2.8.0). Local CLI is 1.15.8, above the `>= 1.10` floor that
  `use_lockfile` requires.
- The three operator-seeded parameters exist and are untouched, all at Version 1:
  `/rebar/prod/jira-url` (String), `/rebar/prod/jira-user` (String),
  `/rebar/prod/jira-api-token` (SecureString). No value was read or printed.
- `/rebar/prod/jira-project` does NOT exist, as expected.
- The declared `jira_project` value `"REB"` matches `rebar.toml` `[jira] project = "REB"`. Verified.

No plan output was ever produced, so the import-block adoption could NOT be checked. The
destroy/recreate/value-overwrite review the operator asked for on those three credential
parameters remains OUTSTANDING and must be done on a real plan before any apply.

## Deliberately not done

- Did not apply anything.
- Did not edit `user_data.sh` to unblock myself.
- Did not create `/rebar/prod/jira-project` by hand via the CLI. That would have satisfied the
  letter of the task while leaving terraform unable to manage it, and would need a fourth import
  block later. The parameter is meant to be terraform-created.
- Did not use any force override.

NEXT STEP: land a one-line-ish fix to `user_data.sh` escaping those three sequences, then re-run
`terraform plan` and review the import adoption before applying.
